_comment: Shared contract file (roadmap C.2). Both tracks read this; change it only
by agreement, because a silent edit invalidates both sides' numbers.
Groups exist for two reasons. (1) H-shifting: demand, energy and grid are
observed quantities that arrive late, so load_master(H) shifts them by
H-1 days. Calendar and weather are known or forecastable for the target
day and are never shifted. (2) swap_weather: only weather_target_day is
replaced when switching from reanalysis to forecast weather.
weather_target_day includes the d_* and *_vs_roll7 columns even though
they are differences against observed history. They are built as
value(T) - something(<T), so the target-day half is forecast at inference
and the column must be rebuilt, not copied, when weather is swapped.
swap_weather handles that; do not move them to weather_lag.
_shift_note: Each of these is shifted by its OWN horizon, from config.H_BY_GROUP -
not uniformly by H. demand and energy come from the Grid-India PSP
report (published D+1, so H=2); grid (sr_*) comes from the
POSOCO/CICERO slice, which runs a further day behind (H=3). Shifting
them uniformly left every sr_*_lag1 column NaN on the row being
predicted - present in training, absent at inference.

weather_swap_rules._comment: How swap_weather rebuilds each kind of weather column.

levels.rule: replace outright with the forecast value for the target day

deltas.rule: forecast(T) - observed(T-1); yesterday is already known at issue time

_comment: Not part of the contract - a measured recommendation Track A may
override. Weather levels are redundant once the autoregressive lags
are present, and trend is actively harmful to trees in an
extrapolating regime. See README 'Choosing features' and baseline.py.
